data.source_period: Study publication 2021; exact observation dates not present in inspected sections
data.source_n: 178 observed triage/initial-assessment cases with completed surveys; eligible adult patients except ESI 1 and specified exclusions
data.source_title: Interruption of initial patient assessment in the emergency department and its effect on patient perception of care quality
data.locator: Abstract; Methods and Results, TIAT observations
data.source_setting: Academic Level I trauma center, Midwestern United States; 55 ED beds, adult ED
data.quantity: Observed triage interruption occurrence and consequence association

value.direction: higher interruption frequency associated with increased errors; interruptions lengthened triage duration

data.unit: percent of observed cases; qualitative associations
data.source_evidence_basis: Prospective time-motion observations found that 62.9% of 178 observations were interrupted one to five times. More interruptions were associated with increased errors, and interruptions increased triage duration; duration was negatively associated with satisfaction. The study separately recorded source, cause, interrupted task, provider reaction, errors, triage duration, and interruption duration.
data.limitations: Single academic site, excludes highest-acuity ESI 1 and several vulnerable/non-English groups; association does not quantify a general causal effect or transferable interruption rate.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Make assessment interruption a possible event that pauses/switches task, tracks unfinished items, and can trigger recheck/rework; avoid assigning this cohort’s frequency to the scenario.
